verdict.summary: Applied Digital has crossed from speculative site developer into a contracted AI datacenter landlord, but the accounting still exposes how much execution sits between signed megawatts and durable equity value. Fiscal Q4 2026 revenue rose 407% to $258.7 million, HPC revenue reached $203.0 million and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was $42.4 million. The portfolio now claims 1,410 MW of contracted critical IT load and $36 billion of initial 15-year contracted revenue, with 175 MW live at Polaris Forge 1. Those are substantial anchors. Yet GAAP net loss attributable to common shareholders was $110.6 million, stock-based compensation in SG&A was $116.8 million, and cash plus restricted cash of $4.2 billion sits against roughly $5.0 billion of debt. Tenant fit-out contributed $152.4 million of quarterly HPC revenue, so headline growth is not equivalent to recurring base rent. APLD deserves credit for leasing traction, not a free pass on construction, customer concentration or dilution. The D+ grade remains fundamental; the stock is only a watch above $26.96.

The 8,393,611 warrant-share registration and preferred structure preserve dilution complexity.

business.overview:
Applied Digital develops and operates high-density campuses, earning recurring base rent, tenant fit-out revenue and expense recoveries from HPC customers; it also retains a smaller datacenter-hosting operation. Revenue depends on commissioned megawatts, lease commencement and construction progress.

The AI transmission channel is direct but physical: hyperscalers and model developers contract critical IT capacity, Applied Digital finances and builds the powered shell, and rent begins as halls are delivered. The $36 billion initial contracted-revenue figure is therefore a long-duration construction and occupancy schedule, not current-period sales.

The model breaks through project delays, cost overruns, unavailable power, tenant concentration or financing terms that shift too much value to creditors and preferred holders. Fit-out revenue can also flatter growth while base rent is still ramping, so segment NOI and delivered MW matter more than consolidated revenue alone. Investors should therefore reconcile recurring base rent, segment operating profit, delivered critical IT load and unrestricted parent liquidity before assigning value to the full contracted-revenue headline.
business.moat: APLD's defensible asset is a portfolio of power-secured, high-density campuses with signed anchor tenants and demonstrated early delivery at Polaris Forge 1. The moat remains project-specific: it can erode through construction slippage, contract renegotiation or a higher cost of capital.

earnings.beatNote: Fiscal Q4 2026 revenue was $258.7M, up 407% YoY. GAAP net loss attributable to common shareholders was $110.6M, or $0.39 per share. Non-GAAP adjusted revenue was $240.4M, adjusted net income was $12.9M, or $0.04 per share, and adjusted EBITDA was $42.4M. HPC revenue of $203.0M included $152.4M of tenant fit-out, while base rent was $44.1M. Management disclosed contracted capacity and delivery milestones rather than formal consolidated revenue guidance. The caveat is quality of growth: fit-out revenue, $116.8M of Q4 stock compensation and construction financing complicate the apparent 407% expansion. No confirmed Applied Digital next-earnings date was available from the official event materials checked.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: APLD is financing a multi-campus build with debt, restricted project cash and equity-linked instruments. The fiscal 2026 filing reports 318.968M non-GAAP diluted weighted-average shares, versus roughly 284.3M point-in-time basic shares. It separately discloses about 7.97M unvested RSUs and 14.39M performance units; 8,393,611 registered warrant shares and the approximately $590M preferred commitment add further legal or variable claims. The preferred conversion cannot be fixed before its contractual settlement inputs are known, so no false fully diluted total is presented. The resale S-3 covers 2.4M warrant shares held by designated purchaser affiliates and provides no issuer resale proceeds. Cash plus restricted cash of $4.2B is project-bound and cannot be freely netted against roughly $5.0B debt.

filings.finding: The February-quarter Form 10-Q establishes Applied Digital's pre-year-end project liquidity, debt and operating baseline; it does not support the later fiscal Q4 revenue or contracted-capacity claims.
The fiscal 2026 Form 10-K reports the year-end balance sheet, contracted campus portfolio and segment economics, including cash plus restricted cash near $4.2B and debt near $5.0B.

The July earnings Form 8-K furnishes fiscal Q4 results, including $258.7M revenue, $203.0M HPC revenue and $42.4M non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA through the official release. This classification controls the editorial conclusion.

This resale Form S-3 registers 2,400,000 common shares issuable on warrants held by designated purchaser affiliates. Applied Digital receives no resale proceeds; it is holder resale registration and potential warrant dilution, not a new primary common-stock sale.
The November 424B3 registers 8,393,611 common shares underlying identified warrants; it evidences potential warrant dilution, not that every warrant was exercised or that cash proceeds were received.
The October S-3ASR supplies automatic shelf capacity across securities classes; the filing alone is neither an ATM program nor evidence of any completed primary or secondary sale.

The October 15 424B3 documents the approximately $590M preferred-equity commitment and its conversion mechanics; it supports a specific equity-linked capital claim, not a generic ATM or straight-debt classification.
The September S-3ASR establishes automatic shelf registration capacity before the later preferred and warrant documents; it does not by itself prove any primary sale, secondary sale or cash proceeds.

contrarianRisks: The 8,393,611 warrant-share registration identifies potential dilution but does not prove exercise.
Preferred financing has equity-conversion economics and should not be collapsed into straight debt.
Restricted project cash is not equivalent to unrestricted parent liquidity.
Tenant concentration makes lease quality dependent on a small number of counterparties.
Fit-out revenue can inflate reported growth before recurring base rent matures.
